A streamline must be tangent to the vector field at every point. In the first quadrant, the arrows point down and to the right. They become more horizontal near the $x$-axis and more vertical near the $y$-axis. The other quadrants have the corresponding reflected pattern.

The matching diagram therefore has hyperbola-shaped branches approaching the coordinate axes in all four quadrants. Along each branch, the tangent has the direction shown by the field.

The horizontal and vertical line families fail where the arrows are diagonal. The parabolas have horizontal tangents on the $y$-axis, where the field is vertical. The ellipses have vertical tangents on the $x$-axis, where the field is horizontal. None of these families matches the field.
